source: The formation and evolution of single germinal centers (GCs) was visualized over days to weeks.

claim: Naïve B cells encounter antigen and form primary foci, which subsequently seed GCs.
source: Naïve B cells encounter antigen and form primary foci, which subsequently seed GCs.

claim: GCs experience widely varying rates of homogenizing selection, even within closely confined spatial proximity.

claim: The scope of targetable locations for intravital imaging has recently expanded to include the spleen in the peritoneal cavity.

claim: The scope of targetable locations for intravital imaging has recently expanded to include the heart within the thoracic cavity.
source: and even the heart within the thoracic cavity (Vinegoni et al., 2015).

claim: A significant gap has remained between the capability for continuous imaging of individual animals on time scales of less than half a day, and the statistically based analysis of timed cohorts of experimental animals on longer time scales.

claim: A discontinuous longitudinal imaging model was recently applied to study dissemination of lymphoma in the murine lymph node.

claim: Adaptive immune responses are crucial to long-lived immunological memory, providing more rapid and effective clearance of previously encountered pathogens.

evidence: The Discussion describes this observation.

claim: High-affinity B cells migrated into the follicle where GCs developed over the course of 12–24 hr after appearing in the paracortical region.
source: and then over the course of the next 12–24 hr migrated into the follicle where GCs developed.
evidence: The Discussion describes this temporal sequence.

claim: Two of eight observed GCs (Fo1 and 4) demonstrated a neat exponential growth phenomenon with doubling time closely approximating the shorter end of past work using mathematical modeling following BrdU labeling.
source: Whereas two of eight observed GCs (Fo1 and 4) demonstrated a neat exponential growth phenomenon with doubling time closely approximating the shorter end of past work using mathematical modeling following BrdU labeling (Table 1, Figure 3—video 1 and Figure 3—video 2 and [Anderson et al., 2009])
evidence: The Discussion describes this observation and cites prior work.

claim: Three GCs demonstrated lower but still reasonable doubling time around ~12 hr (Fo2, 6, and 7).
source: a further three demonstrated lower but still reasonable doubling time around ~12 hr (Fo2, 6, and 7)
evidence: The Discussion describes this observation.

claim: Three GCs demonstrated longer doubling times > 12 hr (Fo3, 5, and 8).
source: and the final three demonstrated longer doubling times > 12 hr (Fo3, 5, and 8).
evidence: The Discussion describes this observation.

claim: In silico analysis of the early response has previously been performed using average rates of division and cell death across multiple explanted GCs for fixed low and high affinity clones.
source: In silico analysis of the early response has previously been performed using average rates of division and cell death across multiple explanted GCs for fixed low and high affinity clones (Anderson et al., 2009).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: In GCs where the B1-8hi clones dominate, the doubling time observed will most closely approximate the 'true' underlying doubling rate as more of the GC is observed.
source: Specifically, in GCs where the B1-8hi clones dominate, the doubling time observed will most closely approximate the 'true' underlying doubling rate as more of the GC is observed.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: In GCs with more competitive clones that are dark, the observed rate may deviate from the true GC dynamics since a greater proportion is unobserved.
source: However, in GCs with more competitive clones that are dark, the observed rate may deviate from the true GC dynamics since a greater proportion is unobserved.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: Cell death as opposed to cell division is the primary effector of affinity-driven selection.
source: As competitive factors and/or GC viability factors begin to affect the dominance of the CFP+ clones, the estimates of doubling time will be artificially elevated, that is slower, as it has been shown that cell death as opposed to cell division is the primary effector of affinity-driven selection (Anderson et al., 2009).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: Within the same lymph node and within the same animal subjected to timed antigen exposure, expansion of primary foci and seeding of GCs, even in adjacent follicles, was found to occur at highly variable rates.
source: Despite this caveat, within the same lymph node and within the same animal subjected to timed antigen exposure, expansion of primary foci and seeding of GCs, even in adjacent follicles, was found to occur at highly variable rates (Table 1).
evidence: The Discussion summarizes this finding and references Table 1.

claim: The black-out phenomenon was observed in three of eight Fo (Fo3, 5, 8).
source: However, several GCs that appeared to have adequate 'seeding' (by comparing relative infiltration of CFP+ cells) later went dark. This black-out phenomenon was observed in three of eight Fo (Fo3, 5, 8)
evidence: The Discussion describes this observation.

claim: The black-out phenomenon is surprising due to the significantly greater baseline affinity of the B1-8hi clones compared to the resting repertoire.
source: which is surprising due to the significantly greater baseline affinity of the B1-8hi clones compared to the resting repertoire
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: The black-out phenomenon may indicate failure to establish a productive GC.
source: and may indicate (i) failure to establish a productive GC
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: The black-out phenomenon may indicate entry of an endogenous dark clone with similar or superior affinity for the antigen and subsequent 'winning-out' of the GC leading to loss of CFP+.
source: (ii) entry of an endogenous dark clone with similar or superior affinity for the antigen and subsequent 'winning-out' of the GC leading to loss of CFP+
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: The black-out phenomenon may indicate that early competition took place and SHM led to the generation of a dark clone with greater affinity than the B1-8hi clones adoptively transferred prior to immunization.
source: or (iii) that early competition took place and SHM led to the generation of a dark clone with greater affinity than the B1-8hi clones adoptively transferred prior to immunization.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: The observation of black-out in multiple GCs followed across time in separate animals deserves further exploration.
source: Nonetheless this observation in multiple GCs followed across time in separate animals deserves further exploration.
evidence: The Discussion suggests future work.

claim: The overall findings were in agreement with previous observations regarding clonal evolution.
source: Combining our intravital imaging approach with the Aicda-Confetti reporter of Tas et al., the process of clonal evolution could be followed over time with single-GC resolution. Again, our overall findings were in agreement with previous observations
evidence: The Discussion compares current findings to prior work.

claim: The longitudinal resolution allowed for additional layers of detail to be uncovered regarding clonal evolution.
source: but the longitudinal resolution allowed for additional layers of detail to be uncovered.
evidence: The Discussion highlights the advantage of the method.

claim: The average clonal evolution towards pauciclonality was found to mask complex underlying processes entailing both clonal bursts and clonal 'inversion events'.
source: The average clonal evolution towards pauciclonality was found to mask complex underlying processes entailing both clonal bursts, as previously reported, but also clonal 'inversion events', whereby a seemingly winning color was suddenly seen to lose competitive momentum allowing for emergence of one or several new colors.
evidence: The Discussion describes this finding.

claim: In the case of a single-color take-over, this event could be reflective of a clonal burst occurring in the new winning color.
source: In the case of a single-color take-over, this event could of course be reflective of a clonal burst occurring in the new winning color
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: The explanation of clonal burst fails to account for multi-color take-overs, since simultaneous clonal bursts are unlikely.
source: whereas this explanation fails to account for multi-color take-overs, since simultaneous clonal bursts are unlikely.
evidence: The Discussion presents this reasoning.

claim: Complex antigens drive permissive clonal selection in GCs.
source: It was recently reported that complex antigens drive permissive clonal selection in GCs (Kuraoka et al., 2016).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: CGG is a more complex mixture of chicken gamma-globulins, which may cater to multiple layers of T follicular helper cells, which could potentially skew responses over time.
source: Although we employed NP-CGG immunizations, where NP would be expected to be the immunodominant epitope on the B cell side, the CGG is a more complex mixture of chicken gamma-globulins, which may cater to multiple layers of T follicular helper cells, which could potentially skew responses over time.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: Chiefly B cells responding to the same antigen or catering to the same T helper cells, would be able to enter an ongoing GC.
source: In this context, it is important to note that chiefly B cells responding to the same antigen or catering to the same T helper cells, would be able to enter an ongoing GC (Schwickert et al., 2007; Schwickert et al., 2009).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: The ARTEMIS model involves a very broad autoreactive repertoire, with increasing epitope spreading over time.
source: This scenario is vastly more complex in the ARTEMIS model, which involves a very broad autoreactive repertoire, with increasing epitope spreading over time (Degn et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: The GC that displayed the prominent sequential dual clonal inversion event, GC H, was at the outset relatively small.
source: Of note, the GC that displayed the prominent sequential dual clonal inversion event, GC H (Figure 5H), was at the outset relatively small
evidence: The Discussion describes this observation and references Figure 5H.

claim: The final take-over by a YFP +mCFP clone in GC H coincided with a decrease in GC size coincident with the latest stages of the GC response.
source: and the final take-over by a YFP +mCFP clone coincided with a decrease in GC size coincident with the latest stages of the GC response.
evidence: The Discussion describes this observation.

claim: It is unclear what determines the size of GCs.
source: It is unclear what determines the size of GCs
evidence: The Discussion identifies an open question.

claim: One could speculate that GC size is related to the degree of successful affinity maturation.
source: One could speculate that it is related to the degree of successful affinity maturation
evidence: The Discussion presents this speculation.

claim: Clonal inversion may be a more likely event in smaller, less successful, GC.
source: and in turn that clonal inversion is a more likely event in smaller, less successful, GC.
evidence: The Discussion presents this speculation.

claim: Studies in both mice and humans demonstrate larger GC structures in AID deficient subjects who have less SHM and affinity maturation.
source: This is supported by studies in both mice and humans that demonstrate larger GC structures in AID deficient subjects who have less SHM and affinity maturation (Fagarasan et al., 2002; Revy et al., 2000).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work supporting this.

claim: The supposition that clonal inversion is more likely in smaller GCs is contraindicated by the clonal inversion event observed in GC G, which was a massive GC.
source: However, this supposition is contraindicated in the present dataset by the clonal inversion event observed in GC G (Figure 5G), which was a massive GC.
evidence: The Discussion presents this counterexample and references Figure 5G.

claim: One could speculate that GCs that homogenize quickly do not 'travel far', and may be suggestive of less affinity matured clones as compared to GC which 'churn' through many clones with mutations accumulating on the way to clonality.
source: Conversely, one could speculate that GCs that homogenize quickly do not 'travel far', and may be suggestive of less affinity matured clones as compared to GC which 'churn' through many clones with mutations accumulating on the way to clonality.
evidence: The Discussion presents this speculation.

claim: Elucidating the question of whether GCs that homogenize quickly are less affinity matured would require an additional in-depth analysis of the mutational landscape across the observed clonal populations.
source: However, elucidating this question would require an additional in-depth analysis of the mutational landscape across the observed clonal populations.
evidence: The Discussion suggests future work.

claim: Autoreactive GC responses were largely reflective of foreign antigen elicited GC clonal dynamics.
source: Finally, our studies were extended to the recently described novel ARTEMIS model for spontaneous autoreactive GCs (Degn et al., 2017) in combination with the Confetti reporter. This revealed that autoreactive GC responses were largely reflective of foreign antigen elicited GC clonal dynamics
evidence: The Discussion summarizes this finding.

claim: The autoreactive GC studies confirmed insights from the foreign antigen GC scenario in an independent model.
source: and confirmed our insights from the foreign antigen GC scenario in an independent model.
evidence: The Discussion summarizes this finding.

claim: It has previously been reported that GCs are open and dynamic structures.
source: It has previously been reported that GCs are open and dynamic structures (Schwickert et al., 2007)
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: Newly activated B cells can enter ongoing GCs.
source: and that newly activated B cells can enter ongoing GCs (Schwickert et al., 2007).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: Whether newly activated B cells entering GCs extends to short-term memory cells, allowing reseeding of GCs in a chronic GC setting remains an open question.
source: Whether this extends to short-term memory cells, allowing reseeding of GCs in a chronic GC setting remains an open question.
evidence: The Discussion identifies an open question.

claim: Secondary remodeling of BCRs of memory B cells has been observed.
source: However, secondary remodeling of BCRs of memory B cells has been observed (McHeyzer-Williams et al., 2015).
evidence: The Discussion cites prior work.

claim: The observation of clonal bursts in one GC followed by emergence of similar colors in neighboring GCs would not occur directly at the GC B cell level, but rather by exit and subsequent reentry of (short-term) memory B cells.
source: Integrating the above-mentioned considerations derived from the available literature, this would not occur directly at the GC B cell level, but rather by exit and subsequent reentry of (short-term) memory B cells.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: At the time-scales presented, reentry of memory B cells would only be expected to occur due to high (auto)antigen levels driving immediate re-engagement of the BCR following GC exit.
source: At the time-scales presented here, this would only be expected to occur due to high (auto)antigen levels driving immediate re-engagement of the BCR following GC exit.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: Future studies employing an Aicda-driven reporter coupled with CD40L-blockade to ablate all ongoing GCs and a subsequent investigation of reporter B cell reentry in reemergent GCs could provide greater clarity on inter-GC communication.
source: Although this remains at present inference, future studies employing an Aicda-driven reporter coupled with CD40L-blockade to ablate all ongoing GCs and a subsequent investigation of reporter B cell reentry in reemergent GCs could provide greater clarity.
evidence: The Discussion suggests future work.

claim: The finding of trafficking between the high-density CFP+ core of dividing cells in the GC and the paracortical clusters between 72–120 hr after immunization may demonstrate a mechanism by which early, pre-GC, competition may influence the clonal composition of the GC.
source: Along the same lines, our finding of trafficking between the high-density CFP+ core of dividing cells in the GC and the paracortical clusters (presumably primary foci) between 72–120 hr after immunization (Figure 3—video 1), may demonstrate a mechanism by which early, pre-GC, competition may influence the clonal composition of the GC
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation and references Figure 3—video 1.

claim: The trafficking between GC and paracortical clusters may contribute to the 'black-out' phenomenon.
source: and may contribute to the 'black-out' phenomenon described above.
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

claim: The most notable differences between sham and window animals were the increase in Gr1 cells in the spleen and the slight, but statistically significant increase in GC B cells in the window node.
source: The most notable differences between sham and window animals were the increase in Gr1 cells in the spleen and the slight, but statistically significant increase in GC B cells in the window node (Figure 2).
evidence: The Discussion summarizes this finding and references Figure 2.

source: The latter finding in particular could be cause for concern in relation to the investigations of clonal dynamics presented here.

source: Two factors could contribute to these differences: 1) the sterile, local inflammation driven by disruption of the overlying tissue, however gentle, and exposure of the underlying tissues
evidence: The Discussion presents this interpretation.

source: and 2) a non-sterile inflammation driven by exposure of the chamber to ambient skin commensals and opportunistic pathogens.

source: We employed broad spectrum perioperative antibiotics in both sham and CLNW animals an effort to reduce the risk of meaningful perturbation further.

source: Additionally, the comparison of clonal evolution in window and contralateral lymph nodes within the same animals, presented in Figure 4, confirmed that this process was not affected by the CLNW.

claim: Any potential GC response associated with the surgical procedure or subsequent contamination of the chamber would be driven by unlabeled clones, which would not directly perturb results.
source: Any potential effect might in part also be alleviated by the experimental setup, whereby immunization (foreign antigen GC) or establishment of autoreactive GCs in the chimeras, and tamoxifen-induced activation of the reporter precedes surgical placement of the window. Therefore, any potential GC response associated with the surgical procedure or subsequent contamination of the chamber (although none such were noted by us in the experiments presented), would be driven by unlabeled clones, which would not directly perturb results.
evidence: The Discussion presents this reasoning.

claim: Outgrowth of a significant body of unlabeled, 'dark' clones would lead to GCs going dark.
source: Indirectly, outgrowth of a significant body of unlabeled, 'dark' clones, targeting ambient antigen (rather than the immunogen NP-CGG, or autoantigen in the autoreactive GC) would instead lead to GCs going dark.

claim: No GCs were observed going dark for the duration of the imaging experiments presented.
source: However, we did not observe any GCs going dark for the duration of the imaging experiments presented here

claim: The GCs that were followed displayed a consistent and robust labeling density, indicating that contamination was not an issue in the presented setup.
source: and the GCs that were followed displayed a consistent and robust labeling density, indicating that this was not an issue in the presented setup.

claim: With the present setup, cellular immune responses can now be followed at a temporal resolution of hours and days and weeks per experimental question at hand.
source: Therefore, with the present setup, cellular immune responses can now be followed at a temporal resolution of hours and days and weeks per experimental question at hand.
